After nearly four years of joint research and development Japanese Scientists working on the Thorium Nuclear Energies Comity have drawn up the designs for a small scale prototype test for the proposed FUJI Molten Salt Thorium Reactor. The finished reactor promises to be capable of substantial power output, competing with modern steam based reactors. For now the small prototype test is predicted to produce a meager 10 MWe of power. Where to put this prototype though has been a matter of debate. Leading officials declared that building the small scale test on the Japanese mainland as a temporary installation would be an egregious waste of money and effort and proposed perhaps building the reactor elsewhere where it may do some good as a more permanent and helpful facility. So naturally the Island of Tuvalu was proposed. Japan wishes to reach out to the government of Tuvalu, asking to procure a section of land for the construction of the small facility. When complete the reactor will provide power to Tuvalu for free.
